newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer fund 96 profit soars to PLN 323 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer fund 96 profit soars to PLN 323 mln.

text.p: The operating profit of the balanced Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund (PPFP), owned by Boston-based Pioneer Group, increased to 323 million zlotys last year from 120 million zloty in 1995, a fund official said.

Pawel Wilkowiecki from the Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company told Reuters on Thursday that some 70 percent of PPFP operational profit came from shares last year, while in 1995 debt instruments were much more profitable.

"We had a 113.5 million zloty profit on shares we sold in 1996, while prices of shares we did not sell increased by 124.4 million, which means we gained 237.9 million from our share portfolio," said Wilkowiecki.

On Wednesday Pioneer said its balanced fund made an 85 million zloty gain though government treasuries and bonds last year. In 1995 Pioneer made 122 million zlotys from debt investment because yields on Polish treasuries were higher.

At the end of 1996 its PPFP fund invested 31.6 percent of its portfolio in shares and rights, 31.7 percent in government bonds, 35.9 percent in treasury bills, 0.4 percent in mass privatisation certificates and 0.4 percent in other instruments.
The value of the balanced fund's participation unit increased by 51 percent to 75.23 zlotys during 1996.
